sim.arch.admin_detail: Daily limits live in the database, so raising 30 to 50 is an admin action, not an app release. Every change is written to the audit log.
sim.arch.admin_never: No admin screen can show the text of a conversation.
sim.arch.android_detail: The same product as an Android input method, plus on-device speech recognition for dictating the instruction.
sim.arch.android_never: Never uploads audio; only recognised text is sent.
sim.arch.auth_detail: Registration is by phone number with a one-time code; admin sessions use PBKDF2 password hashes and server-side session records.
sim.arch.auth_never: Passwords are never stored in plain text, and OTP attempts are rate-limited.
sim.arch.context_detail: The profile is loaded on the server and turned into named data blocks in the prompt: business context, rules, and the user's instruction, each introduced as data rather than as orders.
sim.arch.context_never: A copied message saying 'ignore previous instructions' is quoted, not obeyed.
sim.arch.gateway_detail: One place builds the prompt, calls the provider, counts tokens and estimates cost. Everything the mobile apps see comes through it.
sim.arch.gateway_never: Neither the incoming message nor the generated reply is written anywhere.
sim.arch.ios_detail: The app holds the account and preferences; the keyboard extension does the work inside other apps. They share a keychain group, so signing in once is enough.
sim.arch.ios_never: Holds no provider key and never calls OpenAI.
sim.arch.lede: Select any component to see what it does, where it lives and — just as important — what it never does.
sim.arch.limits_detail: Quota is reserved atomically before OpenAI is called and refunded if the call fails, so parallel requests cannot oversubscribe a plan and a failed reply is never charged.
sim.arch.limits_never: The client's own count is never trusted.
sim.arch.limits_sub: Quota reserved before the provider call
sim.arch.openai_detail: The provider is called from the backend with the key from the server environment. The model is fixed by the server; the client cannot choose it.
sim.arch.openai_never: The key is never present in any app bundle, APK or IPA.
sim.arch.privacy_body: There is no column for it in the schema, no field for it in the admin API, and nothing of it in the logs. A test sends a unique string through the API and fails the build if it appears in the database file, the WAL or the logs.
sim.arch.storage_detail: Accounts, plans, subscriptions, quota counters and usage events. Usage events record length, tokens, latency and status — never content.
sim.arch.storage_never: There is no column for message text.
sim.arch.title: System architecture
sim.arch.transport_detail: Every call carries a short-lived access token. Refresh tokens rotate and reuse is detected, so a stolen token has a small window and leaves a trace.
sim.arch.transport_never: No long-lived token is stored on the device unencrypted.

sim.overview.lede: See how AI Reply turns an incoming customer message into a context-aware reply, straight from the keyboard — on a real backend, with real limits.
sim.overview.p1_body: AI Reply is not another chat app. It is an intelligent layer inside the apps people already use, so nothing about their workflow changes.
sim.overview.p2_body: Tone, audience, language and business context are stored per account and applied to every reply, so the same question gets a different answer for a florist and for a law firm.
sim.overview.p3_body: The app never talks to OpenAI. It talks to the AI Reply backend, which holds the key, enforces the quota and stores no message text at all.
sim.overview.p3_title: The key stays on the server
sim.overview.title: Experience AI Reply

sim.pricing.limits_body: The backend reserves one generation before calling the provider and refunds it if the call fails. The counter resets at local midnight in the server's timezone.

sim.screens.title: Screen by screen
sim.setup.and2: On-screen keyboard → Manage keyboards → AI Reply
sim.setup.and3: Switch to AI Reply from the keyboard selector
sim.setup.and_notice_body: Android warns that any keyboard can collect text. AI Reply sends only the message you copy and the instruction you write, and only when you tap Generate.
sim.setup.full_access_why: Without it the keyboard cannot reach the network, so it cannot ask the backend for a reply. It is used for that and nothing else: what you type is not collected.
sim.setup.ios2: Keyboards → Add New Keyboard → AI Reply
sim.setup.ios3: Tap AI Reply and turn on Allow Full Access
sim.step.insert_panel: The reply is inserted into the messenger's own input field. The user stays in control: edit, then send.
sim.step.keyboard_panel: Tap Generate and a real request goes to the AI Reply backend: quota is reserved, your profile is turned into prompt context, and OpenAI is called server-side.
sim.step.messenger_panel: A generic messenger stands in for WhatsApp, Telegram or Instagram. AI Reply does not replace the messenger — it works inside it.
sim.step.preferences_panel: This is where the product stops being a generic text generator. Everything saved here is sent to the real backend and used in every future prompt.
sim.step.register_body: AI Reply signs you in by phone number. The code arrives in a message.
sim.step.register_note: Twelve countries are supported, including Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan.
sim.step.register_panel: The real app calls the OTP endpoint here. In the simulator the screen is shown as a walkthrough, so that a demo never creates real accounts.
sim.step.setup_body: AI Reply is a keyboard, so it has to be added once in the system settings.
sim.step.setup_panel: iOS and Android both require the keyboard to be enabled once. This screen is the instruction the user follows.
sim.step.verify_body: We sent a four-digit code to
sim.step.verify_panel: Four digits, five attempts, five-minute expiry. Enter any four digits to continue the walkthrough.
sim.step.voice_panel: On Android the instruction can be dictated. Recognition runs on the device — audio never leaves the phone; only the recognised text is sent.
sim.step.welcome_body: Write better replies in seconds, directly from your keyboard.
sim.step.welcome_panel: The first screen of the real app. Nothing is asked for yet — the point is to say what the product does in one line.
sim.title: Product simulator
sim.tour.configure_body: Tone, audience, language and business context. This is what makes the replies yours.
sim.tour.generate_body: One request to the backend: quota, profile, prompt, provider. Usually about a second.
sim.tour.incoming_body: An ordinary message in an ordinary messenger. Copy it — that is the only action the user takes.
sim.tour.insert_body: Edit if you want, insert into the messenger, send. The user always has the last word.
sim.tour.instruction_body: One sentence in your own words: what to say, in what tone, in what language.
sim.tour.limits_body: Every plan has a daily limit, counted on the server and reset at local midnight.
sim.tour.open_body: The keyboard opens above the keys. The conversation stays visible.
sim.tour.pricing_body: Prices and limits live in the database, so they change without shipping a new app.
sim.tour.usage_body: Requests, tokens, cost and plan mix — enough to run the business, with no access to conversations.
sim.usage.explain: Counted by the backend, not the app. The phone's clock cannot buy extra generations.
sim.usage.plan_changed: Plan applied to the demo account.
sim.usage.title: Usage & limits
sim.voice.browser_missing: This browser has no speech recognition. On Android the app uses the system recogniser; here you can type the instruction.
sim.voice.denied_body: Microphone access was declined. You can still type the instruction.
sim.voice.failed: Recognition failed. You can type the instruction instead.
sim.voice.no_speech: Nothing was heard. Try again or type the instruction.
sim.voice.permission_body: Speech is recognised on the device and turned into the instruction text. Audio is never uploaded.
sim.voice.permission_title: Allow AI Reply to record audio?
sim.voice.server_missing: Server-side transcription is not part of the backend: recognition runs on the device, exactly as it does in the Android app.
sim.wf.account_body: The user signs in by phone. Twelve countries are supported and the code expires in five minutes.
sim.wf.account_system: OTP requested, verified, access and refresh tokens issued
sim.wf.configure_body: The profile that will shape every future reply is saved once, on the server.
sim.wf.context_body: Quota is reserved before anything else, then the saved profile becomes named data blocks in the prompt.
sim.wf.copy_body: The copied text is what the reply will be written for. It is capped at 400 characters by default; the admin panel can change that.
sim.wf.copy_system: Text held in memory on the device
sim.wf.draft_body: The draft appears in the keyboard, ready to edit or insert.
sim.wf.edit_body: The generated text is editable before it goes anywhere.
sim.wf.generating_body: The request is in flight: quota reserved, prompt built, provider called.
sim.wf.incoming_body: Nothing about the user's workflow changes: the message arrives where it always did.
sim.wf.incoming_sub: In the messenger the user already uses
sim.wf.insert_body: AI Reply writes into the field the user was already typing in. It does not send anything by itself.
sim.wf.instruction_body: One sentence in the user's own words, up to 400 characters.
sim.wf.instruction_system: Text held in memory on the device
sim.wf.keyboard_on_body: AI Reply is a keyboard, so the system has to be told to allow it.
sim.wf.keyboard_on_component: iOS: Full Access · Android: input method
sim.wf.keyboard_on_system: No backend call — an operating-system setting
sim.wf.open_kbd_body: The panel opens above the keys, so the conversation stays visible.
sim.wf.open_kbd_sub: From the keyboard, without leaving the chat
sim.wf.openai_body: The provider is called from the backend. The model is fixed by the server, and the key never leaves it.
sim.wf.request_body: The keyboard sends the copied message and the instruction to the backend over HTTPS with a short-lived token.
sim.wf.return_body: The response carries the reply and the user's remaining allowance for today.
sim.wf.return_system: Usage event written — metadata only, never text
sim.wf.send_body: The user presses send in their messenger, as always. AI Reply never sends on their behalf.
